text:
Maya: quick follow-up from today's all-hands — can someone clarify the new release cadence and how oncall overlap is supposed to work? specifically: release frequency, freeze windows, and hotfix SLA expectations.
Raj: short recap — weekly minor releases on Tuesdays, monthly majors on the first Tue. freeze window is 2 hours before prod cut for deploy/release jobs. oncall overlap: primary + secondary overlap for 1 hour handoff at shift boundaries.
Elena: thanks! are quality gates changing? do minor releases still require e2e + perf runs?
Sam: tl;dr: automated smoke + unit tests are mandatory pre-merge. e2e + perf run during canary for minors; full e2e + perf required for majors. exceptions if a change touches runtime or serving infra — then skip is not allowed.
Sam: link to process doc: https://go.redwood/release-process (section 3 covers gates)
Kofi: for hotfixes — what's the SLA we commit to customer teams?
Priya: P0 customer-impacting regression: aim for 2h response and 6h rollback or fix window. internal target for non-customer P1/P2 fixes is 24–72h depending on severity. these are operational targets, not billing SLAs.
Maya: do we have guidance for when to bypass weekly cadence for urgent fixes?
Raj: yes — use the emergency release flow (see playbook). approval from EngOps + oncall lead required, and release-bot will create an emergency pipeline.
release-bot: Emergency release workflow triggered by @Raj. Please confirm approvers and leave a short reason. :rotating_light:
Priya: emergency-release checklist (condensed):
```
1) Triage + tag commit with emergency-release
2) Notify customer-impact channel + PMs
3) Run smoke and the minimal rollback test
4) Deploy to canary and wait 10m signals
5) If green, promote to prod. If not, rollback and open incident.
```
Elena: who owns post-release verification for the weekly minors? is it the deploy owner or oncall?
Sam: deploy owner owns verification for their change for the first 30m; oncall owns platform-level metrics for the 2h post-release window. if anything looks off, oncall coordinates rollback.
Kofi: are SLAs documented somewhere central? ops-legal asked for a short blurb to include in contract templates.
Priya: yes, see https://go.redwood/sla-summary — includes MTTR targets, uptime buckets, and escalation contacts. i'll follow up with a 1-paragraph summary for legal.
Maya: ok this helps. small ask: can someone create a short one-pager for the eng handbook about the new cadence + emergency flow? engineers are already asking.
Raj: will do, pulling from the doc and playbook. ETA EOD tomorrow.
Maya: perfect — thanks everyone :raised_hands:
